claims.text: Disimpaction may need oral, oral then rectal, or rectal then oral tx; some children need only laxatives (⍉enemas or suppositories).
claims.quote: Disimpaction may require oral treatment, oral and then rectal treatment, or rectal and then oral treatment. Some children are given only laxatives and do not need enemas or suppositories.

claims.text: Often used: PEG w lytes (± a stimulant laxative, eg, bisacodyl, senna), or saline enemas + a 2-wk regimen of oral agents and suppositories.
claims.quote: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) with electrolytes, sometimes in conjunction with a stimulant laxative (eg, bisacodyl, senna), or a sequence of saline enemas plus a 2-week regimen of oral agents (eg, bisacodyl tablets) and suppositories are often used.

claims.text: Maintenance: PEG w.o lytes = used most often, titrated to 1 to 2 semisoft stools a day;
claims.quote: There are many options for maintenance laxative therapy (see table Treatment of Constipation in Children), but PEG without electrolytes is used most often, titrated to effect (eg, 1 to 2 semisoft stools a day).

claims.text: then slow w.draw of laxatives once Sx resolve.
claims.quote: Bowel retraining is a long process that may take months to years and includes slow withdrawal of laxatives once symptoms resolve and continued encouragement of toilet sitting.

claims.text: Glycerin suppository, infants and children < 2 y: 1/2–1 pediatric suppository once/day for up to 3 days.
claims.quote: Glycerin suppositories Infants and children < 2 years: 1/2–1 pediatric suppository once/day for up to 3 days
